title: Beyond the 956: Pregnant inmate Rebecca Taylor escapes in prison transport vehicle after Whataburger stop in Albuquerque
excerpt: Rebecca Taylor, 26, allegedly took control of a New Mexico corrections transport vehicle during a stop at a Whataburger in Albuquerque on Wednesday, November 25, 2026, and drove away while officers were outside the vehicle. The vehicle was later found by GPS, but Taylor remained at large on Thursday as a multi-agency search continued.
content:
🌎 BEYOND THE 956

A 26-year-old pregnant inmate is on the run in New Mexico after she allegedly stole the corrections transport vehicle carrying her — during a stop for food at a Whataburger in Albuquerque.

Rebecca Taylor was being transported back to the Western New Mexico Correctional Facility in Grants after a prenatal appointment in Albuquerque on Wednesday morning, November 25, 2026, according to the New Mexico Corrections Department. Around 11:35 a.m., the three-officer transport team stopped at a Whataburger on 98th Street NW. Taylor, who was not restrained because she is in the second trimester of her pregnancy, allegedly unbuckled herself, climbed into the driver’s seat of the Dodge Journey transport vehicle and drove away while an officer was standing outside the vehicle.

A second inmate who was also in the vehicle was able to get out as Taylor drove off and is back in custody, officials said.

Taylor was serving a six-year sentence after pleading guilty to four counts stemming from a series of vehicle thefts dating to 2024, according to court records cited by The Associated Press.

The transport vehicle was found about an hour later, around 12:30 p.m., through GPS near Crestview Drive SW in southwest Albuquerque — but Taylor was not inside, the department said. Her orange prison jumpsuit was later found discarded near the intersection of 98th Street and Rio Bravo Boulevard, and a cellphone belonging to the transport team was found near Alamosa Park.

A multi-agency search continued on Thursday, November 26, and the corrections department said Taylor still had not been found. All New Mexico prisons went into lockdown after the escape; the statewide lockdown was lifted at 6 a.m. Thursday. Officials said Taylor has ties to Cleveland and Houston, Texas, and the Albuquerque area, and warned the public not to approach her but to call 911 if she is seen.

Taylor is presumed innocent of any new charges unless proven guilty in court.

Update — November 27, 2026

The U.S. Marshals Service has joined the multi-agency search for Taylor and is offering a reward of up to $5,000 for information leading to her arrest, CBS News reported. The New Mexico Corrections Department shared the Marshals Service wanted poster, which identifies her as Rebecca Louise Taylor, 26, wanted for escape, and describes her as 5 feet 7 inches tall and 180 pounds, with red hair and blue eyes, warning the public not to approach her. The state Probation and Parole Division issued an arrest warrant for Taylor on November 25, the day of the escape, according to ABQ Raw. As of Friday afternoon, November 27, Taylor remained at large, with authorities checking bus and train stations in Albuquerque, according to USA Today. Anyone with information is asked to call 911 or the U.S. Marshals Service tip line at 1-877-926-8332.

Sources: WorldStar (@worldstar); People; BBC; The Associated Press; KOAT. Update sources: CBS News; FOX 26 Houston; USA Today; ABQ Raw; New Mexico Corrections Department (Nov. 27, 2026).
